acceptance_signals: A new repository-owned pilot record identifies historical Taxi adoption commit 8145376ed31f58f6261591a3db74ac6c2387cd76 and the current read-only governance result PASS=17 WARN=1 FAIL=0 ADVISORY=4 without storing a machine-specific source path, Taxi code, data, credentials, workflows, or business policy.

The record distinguishes the historical adoption observation from the current read-only check and states that timed start, timed stop, and elapsed duration were not recorded, so no ten-minute or unassisted-pass claim is made.

Observed assistance and friction are limited to evidence already preserved in dated starter records, including nested Windows path, active-environment, command-syntax, stale-environment, and successful-check-versus-complete-governance interpretation friction.

The record names the historical maintainer decisions later resolved in Taxi and records the human-selected current disposition: the empty dependency graph is complete only for the current single declared capability; artifact tracking is deferred for lack of demonstrated need; the artifact WARN remains honest and non-blocking.

Deterministic contract and check results are separated from advisory claims about real-world completeness, control effectiveness, dependency completeness, artifact value, benefit, and general usability.

The prepared semantic-relation gap-analysis template remains unfilled, and no semantic schema, checker, report field, AgentGov behavior, Taxi file, external system, Git history, release, or deployment is changed.

DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md, STATUS.md, the source-boundary map, and the 2026-08-23 development log consistently describe the record as a closed historical evidence account with unavailable timing rather than a successful ten-minute pilot.
Documentation tests protect the commit identity, timing boundary, conservative maintainer decision, current counts, privacy boundary, and unchanged semantic-gap status.

Focused and full tests, repository governance, task scope reconciliation, JSON parsing, privacy-bounded content checks, and git diff validation pass or retain only documented pre-existing unrelated findings.

decision.rationale: The accountable human reviewed structured proposal prp-44c07c2cc45a4139a5bed829b91ba789 and admitted that exact task through an explicit admission control.

requirement.summary: Create one sanitized historical Taxi cross-domain adoption record from verified starter and read-only Taxi repository evidence; disclose that strict start, stop, and elapsed timing are unavailable and support no ten-minute claim; record observed assistance and friction, the resolved historical maintainer decisions, and the human-selected conservative disposition that the empty dependency graph is complete only for the current single declared capability while tracked artifact configuration is deferred and its WARN retained; update the owning strategic, current-status, dated-evidence, source-boundary, and documentation-test surfaces without modifying Taxi or changing AgentGov behavior.

items: A historical record could accidentally imply that the adoption commit timestamp measures pilot duration.
Combining historical and current observations could misstate which AgentGov version produced each result.
A machine-specific source path, private repository detail, Taxi business content, or secret-like string could leak into the starter record.
The human dependency and artifact disposition could be overstated as a deterministic completeness finding or a permanent cross-project policy.
Closing the evidence record could be confused with proving the ten-minute adoption goal or completing the later development-loop shadow pilot.
Status and strategic documents could diverge if only one owning surface is updated.
Reviewed assumption: The historical Taxi adoption commit and starter development logs are authoritative for what was changed and what friction was observed.
Reviewed assumption: The current read-only Taxi repository check is supporting present-state evidence and is not presented as the historical adoption result.
Reviewed assumption: The accountable product owner is also authorized to record the stated conservative maintainer disposition for this bounded starter-kit evidence closeout.
Reviewed assumption: A recorded unavailable timing state satisfies evidence closure while invalidating any strict ten-minute performance claim.
Reviewed assumption: Deferring optional artifact tracking and retaining its WARN is preferable to implementing an artifact without a demonstrated retained-artifact and review need.
Reviewed unknown: Exact timed start, timed stop, and elapsed duration for the 2026-07-24 Taxi adoption are unavailable.
Reviewed unknown: Whether tracked Taxi capability artifacts would provide enough future review value to justify their maintenance cost remains unknown.
Reviewed unknown: Whether the adoption experience and conservative disposition generalize to other repositories or maintainers remains unknown.

title: Close the historical Taxi cross-domain pilot record
